newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SENTENCE DEFERRED ON TRIPLE DRUGS OFFENDER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SENTENCE DEFERRED ON TRIPLE DRUGS OFFENDER.

text.p: Charlton Athletic midfielder Jay Notley, who admitted taking cannabis, cocaine and Ecstacy, has been given three months to rescue his soccer career after the English F.A. deferred sentence on Monday for his triple drugs offence.
Notley, 18, was caught by a mobile doping unit at the London first division club's training ground at the start of November.

The F.A. disciplinary commission dealing with Notley's case took his age into account and opted to defer sentence for three months while he undergoes rehabilitation and counselling. He will not be allowed to play during that time.

Charlton manager Alan Curbishley said: "No other club has done as much as us to try and curb the problem of drugs. They took into account the fact that Jay has lost his way a little bit and is very remorseful."
